name: Tarot de Marseille (Public Domain)

sections.Summary: Starting without certainty—choosing curiosity over control.
sections.Reversed: Impulsivity or avoidance. If you’re calling it “freedom,” check whether it’s actually escape. Slow down: name the real fear, then choose one responsible next step.
sections.Interpretation: A new chapter wants a lighter grip. Notice the urge to predict outcomes; try a small, values-aligned experiment instead. Ask what you would do if you were allowed to be a beginner.

sections.Summary: You have enough to begin—focus converts intention into action.
sections.Reversed: Scattered effort or self-deception (“I can’t” / “it’s pointless”). Identify the distortion, then pick a 10-minute proof-of-ability action.
sections.Interpretation: Clarify one goal and one next action. The mind may be overthinking; return to what is controllable: attention, effort, and practice. Choose a simple plan and execute.

sections.Summary: Listening beneath the noise—your body and dreams carry data.
sections.Reversed: Second-guessing or numbness. If you feel “nothing,” check for overload. Reduce input, restore sleep, and ask for one gentle truth at a time.
sections.Interpretation: Before problem-solving, gather signals: feelings, sensations, patterns. Let the answer emerge by observing rather than forcing. Journal: what do I already know but don’t want to admit?

sections.Summary: What you nurture grows—start with your own inner ecosystem.
sections.Reversed: Overgiving, depletion, or creative blockage. Practice boundaries: say no to one drain; say yes to one replenishing act today.
sections.Interpretation: Support the conditions for thriving: rest, food, time, affection, beauty. If you’re stuck, shift from self-critique to self-care and watch motivation return.

sections.Summary: Stability is built—clear rules reduce anxiety.
sections.Reversed: Rigidity or power struggles. If control is the coping strategy, practice flexibility: ask what outcome matters most and loosen everything else.
sections.Interpretation: Choose structure that supports your values: schedules, limits, roles, agreements. Where life feels chaotic, create one simple rule and follow it for a week.

sections.Summary: Guidance and shared meaning—learn the rule before you break it.
sections.Reversed: Dogma or rebellion for rebellion’s sake. If you’re rejecting everything, ask what you still need: belonging, purpose, or clarity—and meet it directly.
sections.Interpretation: Name the value beneath the rule. Seek a teacher, model, or method that aligns with your ethics. Practice consistency: small rituals create stability.

sections.Summary: A decision guided by values—choose what you can stand behind.
sections.Reversed: Avoidance of commitment or self-betrayal. Watch for “shoulds” and people-pleasing. Practice one honest conversation or one honest boundary.
sections.Interpretation: This is about alignment: head, heart, and behavior. If you feel torn, list your values and choose the option that best honors them (not the one that reduces anxiety fastest).

sections.Summary: Steer your life with intention—two forces can be harnessed.
sections.Reversed: Burnout, aggression, or drifting. If you’re pushing too hard, rest and re-aim. If you’re drifting, define one measurable weekly target.
sections.Interpretation: Pick a direction and commit to daily practice. Motivation follows action. When inner parts conflict, negotiate: what does each part need to cooperate?

sections.Summary: Reality-testing—what’s true, what’s fair, what’s the next right step?
sections.Reversed: Rationalization or denial. If you’re telling a story to protect your ego, gently return to truth. Own one small responsibility today.
sections.Interpretation: Separate facts from interpretations. Make amends where needed, and make decisions you can defend with integrity. Consider: what would be fair to all parts of me?

sections.Summary: Step back to see clearly—quiet reveals what noise hides.
sections.Reversed: Isolation or avoidance disguised as “self-care.” Reconnect to one trusted person or one supportive routine.
sections.Interpretation: Reduce stimulation. Ask: what’s the essential problem? What’s the essential value? Take one small step with calm consistency.

sections.Reversed: Resistance to change. If you’re stuck, loosen your grip: change one routine, one thought, or one environment cue.
sections.Interpretation: Notice patterns: what repeats? Instead of asking “why me?”, ask “what’s my leverage point?” Choose one adaptive behavior for this phase.

sections.Reversed: Self-doubt or reactive anger. Practice a pause: breathe, name the feeling, choose a response that matches your values.
sections.Interpretation: Work with your emotions, not against them. Validate the feeling, then choose the behavior. Courage can be slow, kind, and consistent.

sections.Summary: A deliberate pause to see differently.
sections.Reversed: Stuckness or martyrdom. If you’re sacrificing without meaning, renegotiate. Take one action that restores agency.
sections.Interpretation: Try a cognitive reframe: what else could this mean? Release the need to “solve” right now. Choose acceptance of what you cannot change this week.

sections.Summary: Letting go so life can reorganize.
sections.Reversed: Clinging and avoidance. If you’re postponing the inevitable, take one tiny step toward closure (a message, a plan, a boundary).
sections.Interpretation: Name what is over. Grieve cleanly. Then ask: what does this ending make possible? Pick one small “closing ritual” and one “opening action.”

sections.Reversed: Extremes or dysregulation. Identify triggers and add one stabilizer (food, water, rest, a break, a boundary).
sections.Interpretation: Choose the middle path. Combine supports: sleep + movement + social connection + meaning. Replace all-or-nothing thinking with “both/and.”

sections.Reversed: Liberation and honesty. Name the pattern, ask for support, and take one concrete boundary step (remove a cue, add friction, add help).
sections.Interpretation: Notice what you use to numb, avoid, or prove worth. Replace shame with curiosity: what need is this trying to meet? Choose a healthier substitute.

sections.Summary: A false structure collapses—painful, but clarifying.
sections.Reversed: Avoided change. If you keep patching a rotten foundation, choose one honest conversation or one decisive action to prevent a bigger crash.
sections.Interpretation: If something is breaking, it may have been unsustainable. Stabilize: breathe, simplify, seek support, and do the next right thing in small pieces.

sections.Summary: Gentle optimism—evidence that recovery is possible.
sections.Reversed: Discouragement. Treat hope like a muscle: do one tiny action that future-you would thank you for.
sections.Interpretation: Look for what’s working. Build hope through action: one supportive habit, one kind connection, one step toward meaning.

sections.Summary: The mind fills gaps—test assumptions gently.
sections.Reversed: Emerging clarity. Reduce avoidance: take one small action that brings information (ask, check, measure, write it down).
sections.Interpretation: When clarity is low, the brain imagines worst cases. Reality-test: what do I know vs. what am I guessing? Ground in body and facts.

sections.Summary: Warmth and truth—life feels simpler in the light.
sections.Reversed: Clouded joy or harsh self-criticism. Practice gratitude + realism: list three facts of progress, even if small.
sections.Interpretation: Name what is going well and amplify it. Share credit, enjoy progress, and let play be part of healing.

sections.Summary: An honest review—choose growth over shame.
sections.Reversed: Self-condemnation or avoidance of truth. Replace “I am bad” with “I did something I regret; I can repair and learn.”
sections.Interpretation: Take inventory without self-attack. What did you learn? What will you do differently? Make amends and recommit to values.

sections.Summary: A cycle completes—integrate the lesson and carry it forward.
sections.Reversed: Loose ends or fear of finishing. Pick one unfinished task and close it this week; closure restores energy.
sections.Interpretation: Celebrate completion and harvest meaning. Identify what you’re taking into the next chapter (skills, boundaries, relationships, identity).

sections.Summary: A new impulse to create or act.
sections.Reversed: Energy is blocked—check sleep, fear of failure, or perfectionism. Lower the bar and begin anyway.
sections.Interpretation: Start small: one action that proves momentum. Treat motivation as something you build through doing.

sections.Reversed: Indecision or playing it safe. Ask: what would I choose if I trusted myself 10% more?
sections.Interpretation: Pick a direction and define your first milestone. Choose breadth or depth—don’t try to do everything at once.

sections.Reversed: Delays or doubt. Improve the system (schedule, tracking, accountability) instead of questioning your worth.
sections.Interpretation: Your effort is working. Stay consistent and widen support: ask for help, resources, or feedback.

sections.Summary: A safe base and shared joy.
sections.Reversed: Tension at home or instability. Repair with clear agreements and one act of warmth.
sections.Interpretation: Celebrate a milestone. Strengthen routines that create safety and connection.

sections.Reversed: Avoidance or suppressed resentment. Have the honest talk—short, respectful, and specific.
sections.Interpretation: Name the real need underneath the conflict. Compete with your past self, not others.

sections.Reversed: Imposter feelings or needing applause. Anchor in internal metrics and values, not external validation.
sections.Interpretation: Receive praise without minimizing. Let success update your self-story: evidence that you can do hard things.

sections.Reversed: Overwhelm. Simplify: choose one battle, one boundary, one next step.
sections.Interpretation: Protect your priorities. Say no to distractions and yes to the work that matters.

sections.Reversed: Delays or chaos. Reduce inputs and re-prioritize; don’t confuse urgency with importance.
sections.Interpretation: Act while the window is open. Communicate clearly and keep it simple.

sections.Reversed: Burnout. Ask for help, reduce load, and rebuild boundaries before you push again.
sections.Interpretation: You’re close. Rest strategically, then continue. Protect recovery like it’s part of the plan.

sections.Reversed: Avoiding responsibility or collapsing. Break tasks into micro-steps and ask for support.
sections.Interpretation: Audit commitments. Delegate, automate, or drop one thing. Capacity is a resource to manage.

sections.Reversed: Inconsistency. Choose one project and give it a two-week trial before switching.
sections.Interpretation: Experiment and learn by doing. Treat mistakes as data, not verdicts.

sections.Reversed: Impulsivity. Add one pause: confirm your goal, then act with precision.
sections.Interpretation: Use your energy to take a clear action now. Courage grows when you follow through.

sections.Reversed: Self-doubt or comparison. Return to your own lane; measure progress against your values.
sections.Interpretation: Lead with warmth. Encourage yourself the way you’d encourage a friend.

sections.Reversed: Ego or dominance. Ask: am I leading from values or from fear of losing control?
sections.Interpretation: Choose a direction and align others through clarity and purpose. Make the plan simple and repeatable.

sections.Reversed: Emotional blockage. Name the feeling and its need; create one safe outlet (talk, write, cry, move).
sections.Interpretation: Let yourself feel. Share honestly, receive support, and practice kindness toward your inner world.

sections.Reversed: Imbalance. Ask: am I overgiving, under-communicating, or avoiding vulnerability?
sections.Interpretation: Choose reciprocity. Practice a clear request, a clear boundary, or a sincere repair attempt.

sections.Reversed: Overindulgence or feeling left out. Choose one nourishing connection over shallow social noise.
sections.Interpretation: Reach out. Celebrate progress with people who uplift you.

sections.Reversed: Restlessness. Try a values check: what do I want that I’m afraid to want?
sections.Interpretation: Notice what you’re dismissing. Small pleasures and small supports count—practice receptive attention.

sections.Reversed: Avoided grief or stuck rumination. Schedule a bounded grief practice (10 minutes), then do one restorative action.
sections.Interpretation: Validate the loss without turning it into a global story about you. Grieve, then identify what remains and what can be rebuilt.

sections.Reversed: Living in the past. Keep the lesson, release the longing. Choose one present-moment joy today.
sections.Interpretation: Reconnect with what made you feel safe and alive. Offer simple kindness—especially to your younger self.

sections.Reversed: Escapism. Replace fantasizing with one concrete step that creates real change.
sections.Interpretation: Limit choices and pick the one aligned with values. “Perfect” is a trap; choose “good enough + consistent.”

sections.Reversed: Avoidance or fear of change. Identify the specific discomfort you’re avoiding and face it gently, in pieces.
sections.Interpretation: Practice healthy detachment. If something consistently violates your values, plan an exit and take one step today.

sections.Reversed: Hollow satisfaction. If pleasure isn’t landing, check for burnout, shame, or unmet needs.
sections.Interpretation: Receive what you’ve earned. Practice savoring without guilt; it rewires the brain toward safety.

sections.Summary: Shared wellbeing through values and repair.
sections.Reversed: Tension at home. Focus on repair: one honest conversation, one boundary, one shared ritual.
sections.Interpretation: Prioritize the relationships and routines that create peace. Name appreciation out loud.

sections.Summary: A tender message from the heart.
sections.Reversed: Emotional immaturity or avoidance. Practice naming one feeling + one need without drama.
sections.Interpretation: Let yourself be moved. Express feelings simply and kindly.

sections.Reversed: Moodiness or fantasy. Reality-test your story; act on facts, not longing alone.
sections.Interpretation: Make the offer, write the note, start the art. Keep it grounded with one practical step.

sections.Reversed: Over-empathy or enmeshment. Return to boundaries and self-care; you can be kind without absorbing everything.
sections.Interpretation: Hold space for feelings (yours and others) without drowning in them. Care is not the same as fixing.

sections.Reversed: Emotional manipulation or shutdown. Reconnect: name what you feel, then choose a respectful action.
sections.Interpretation: Regulate first, decide second. Lead with calm honesty and repair when needed.

sections.Summary: A clean thought cuts through confusion.
sections.Reversed: Mental fog or harsh self-talk. Replace absolute judgments with specific, testable statements.
sections.Interpretation: Define the problem in one sentence. Then choose one decisive action aligned with that truth.

sections.Reversed: Overthinking. Set a deadline and pick the “least regrettable” option.
sections.Interpretation: Gather missing data, then decide. Avoiding the decision is still a decision—choose consciously.

sections.Summary: Pain asks for honesty and healing.
sections.Reversed: Healing is underway—or denial persists. Choose one repair step: apologize, grieve, or seek support.
sections.Interpretation: Name the loss and the meaning you assigned to it. Separate the event from the global belief it triggered.

sections.Reversed: Restlessness or burnout. Put rest on the calendar and protect it.
sections.Interpretation: Pause to restore cognition and mood. Sleep and stillness are interventions, not indulgences.

sections.Reversed: Aftermath and regret. Make amends or release the fight; let dignity replace dominance.
sections.Interpretation: Check motives: do you want to be right or to be well? Choose repair, boundaries, or disengagement wisely.

sections.Reversed: Dragging old patterns forward. Identify one belief or behavior to leave behind intentionally.
sections.Interpretation: Choose the next environment, habit, or relationship pattern that reduces harm. Accept help; transitions are easier with support.

sections.Reversed: Truth emerges. Come clean, simplify, and rebuild trust through consistent action.
sections.Interpretation: Be strategic, but not dishonest. Ask: where am I avoiding discomfort and calling it “smart”?

sections.Reversed: Release is possible. Ask: what one action would prove I have choices?
sections.Interpretation: Identify the limiting belief (“I can’t / I’m not allowed / it’s too late”). Test it with one small behavioral experiment.

sections.Reversed: Relief begins when you ask for help. Share one fear with a trusted person or professional support.
sections.Interpretation: Write worries down; separate solvable vs. unsolvable. Do one coping skill (breathing, grounding, problem plan).

sections.Reversed: Slow healing. Avoid repeating the story; build a new routine that supports your nervous system.
sections.Interpretation: Stop fighting what is already over. Let this be closure. Then choose the smallest next step toward recovery.

sections.Reversed: Gossip or mental agitation. Channel the energy into study, journaling, or a direct conversation.
sections.Interpretation: Investigate assumptions. Use curiosity to reduce fear and increase clarity.

sections.Reversed: Rushing, harshness, or tunnel vision. Add one pause to check impact and accuracy.
sections.Interpretation: Speak clearly and take decisive action. Keep the goal in view; don’t fight the wrong battle.

sections.Reversed: Bitterness or defensiveness. Soften the story: what hurt am I protecting? Choose one compassionate reframe.
sections.Interpretation: Name what is true and set boundaries without cruelty. Respect your intelligence and your tenderness.

sections.Reversed: Coldness or misuse of authority. Balance logic with empathy; check how power is being used.
sections.Interpretation: Make decisions based on data and values. Communicate standards clearly and follow them consistently.

sections.Reversed: Missed opportunity or fear of investing. Take one small, low-risk step to build confidence.
sections.Interpretation: Start the habit, budget, or craft. Practical consistency beats bursts of effort.

sections.Reversed: Overwhelm. Reduce commitments; pick one nonessential thing to drop this week.
sections.Interpretation: Set priorities and build a flexible plan. Ask: what can I simplify or postpone?

sections.Summary: Skill grows with support and feedback.
sections.Reversed: Misalignment. Clarify roles, expectations, and the definition of “done.”
sections.Interpretation: Invite collaboration. Improve the system, not just effort. Ask for one specific piece of feedback.

sections.Reversed: Clinging or scarcity thinking. Practice one act of trust—share, invest, or ask for support.
sections.Interpretation: Build healthy security (budget, boundaries, routines). Keep generosity alive: security isn’t the same as fear.

sections.Reversed: Recovery begins. Accept help and rebuild step-by-step—one bill, one meal, one plan at a time.
sections.Interpretation: Name needs clearly. Seek resources, community, and practical support. Shame isolates; connection heals.

sections.Reversed: Strings attached or imbalance. Renegotiate: what’s fair, what’s sustainable, what’s respectful?
sections.Interpretation: Practice healthy reciprocity. Give with consent, receive without shame, and clarify terms to prevent resentment.

sections.Reversed: Frustration. If results lag, change the method (not your worth).
sections.Interpretation: Review what’s working and adjust. Stay consistent; don’t quit in the slow middle.

sections.Reversed: Perfectionism or boredom. Reconnect to meaning, or redesign the practice to be sustainable.
sections.Interpretation: Commit to deliberate practice. Track small improvements; let process be the reward.

sections.Reversed: Insecurity despite success. Check the belief: “I’ll lose it.” Build a plan, not a panic.
sections.Interpretation: Savor what you’ve built. Strengthen systems that maintain wellbeing (money, health, home).

sections.Reversed: Fragile foundations. Simplify finances, clarify agreements, and repair family patterns where possible.
sections.Interpretation: Invest in what lasts: relationships, skills, health, and aligned structures.

sections.Reversed: Procrastination. Reduce the task to a 5-minute start and begin now.
sections.Interpretation: Study, budget, train, or apprentice. Small consistent steps beat big bursts.

sections.Reversed: Stuck in routine or stubbornness. Adjust one habit to restore flexibility.
sections.Interpretation: Do the next right thing—daily. Build a routine that makes success boring and inevitable.

sections.Reversed: Over-functioning. Let others contribute; your care must include you.
sections.Interpretation: Support life through practical kindness: food, rest, money, and a calm home base.

sections.Reversed: Greed or fear-based control. Practice generosity and transparency; loosen the grip.
sections.Interpretation: Lead by building sustainable systems. Make financial and health decisions aligned with values.

description:
A public-domain Tarot de Marseille-style deck intended for reflective, non-predictive readings.

This deck is designed for an app experience where the “reader” behaves more like a CBT-informed guide than a fortune-teller: each card becomes a prompt to examine thoughts, feelings, behaviors, and core beliefs. Upright meanings emphasize adaptive interpretations and constructive actions; reversed meanings point to cognitive distortions, avoidance patterns, emotional blocks, or rigid coping strategies.

Artwork sources are public-domain Marseille-style card scans available on Wikimedia Commons (many from late-19th-century Gallica/BnF sources and the Conver tradition). Image URLs use Wikimedia’s stable file redirect endpoint (Special:FilePath) so your client can fetch images directly.

Use suggestion (CBT-friendly): When a card appears, ask: (1) What story is my mind telling? (2) What evidence supports/contradicts it? (3) What value-aligned micro-step can I take in the next 24 hours?
